title: Michelson v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC dismissed the complaint as not judicially in order and incurable under the Rules of Discipline because it failed to identify any act or decision of the lower court under BCO 43-1; the objections concerned congregational actions, and the BCO has no provision for complaint against a congregation. The dissent would have found the complaint judicially in order as to the Session’s calling and recommending the congregational meeting and assigned it to a panel.
first_summary: The SJC dismissed the Michelsons’ complaint against Northwest Georgia Presbytery as not judicially in order. The complaint challenged the congregational meeting’s election of three assistant pastors as associate pastors without a pulpit committee, ballots, or abstention counting. The SJC held the complaint failed BCO 43-1 because it did not identify any act or decision of the Session; the only Session act was calling the meeting, and the BCO allows no complaint against congregational action. The dissent would find the Session’s calling and recommendation justiciable.
summary: The Michelsons’ complaint challenged a congregational meeting’s procedure for electing three assistant pastors as associate pastors—allegedly without a pulpit committee, ballots, counted abstentions, or protection for a substantial minority. The SJC dismissed it as not judicially in order: BCO 43-1 requires complaint against an act or decision of a court, but the complaint attacked congregational actions, while the Session’s only act was calling the meeting and was not objected to. The SJC noted other possible redress; the dissent found the Session’s call and recommendation justiciable.
